title: Osmosis across a semi-permeable membrane

bodies.name: Membrane
bodies.label: Semi-permeable membrane
bodies.describe: Pores let water molecules through but not the larger solute molecules.

lessons.title: Watch the water move
lessons.text: Water molecules cross the pores in both directions; solute molecules bounce off the membrane on the right. Wait for the net-flow event.
lessons.explain: Solute that cannot enter the pores lowers the water's chemical potential on its side, so the net flow runs into the solution. In real membranes this is mostly bulk flow through the pores, not water simply "diffusing down its own gradient" (Kramer & Myers 2013); the particle picture here shows the direction and the balance, not the molecular mechanism.

lessons.title: Equilibrium
lessons.text: The right level rises until its extra pressure pushes water back as fast as it arrives. Wait for equilibrium.
lessons.explain: The height difference at equilibrium measures the osmotic pressure; it grows with solute concentration (van 't Hoff: π ≈ cRT).

lessons.title: More solute
lessons.text: Double the solute. The tank refills from scratch and settles at a bigger height difference.
lessons.explain: Osmotic pressure rises with the number of dissolved particles.

lessons.title: Pure water both sides
lessons.text: Remove all solute: nothing drives a net flow and the levels stay equal.
lessons.explain: Osmosis needs a concentration difference across a membrane that blocks the solute.
